newsitem.title: USA: PIA Merchandising sees Q1 oper loss.
newsitem.headline: PIA Merchandising sees Q1 oper loss.

text.p: PIA Merchandising Services Inc on Thursday said it expected to report a first-quarter operating loss of between $0.17 and $0.20 a share versus net income of $0.18 a share one year ago.
First-quarter revenues are expected to rise to about $28 million from $26 million in the year-ago quarter.

In a statement, PIA said it saw operating results for all of 1997 falling "substantially" short of its year-earlier results despite increasing revenue. "The expected decline in profitability for the quarter and the year is due in part to a shift in the mix of business," the company said.

PIA, a provider of nationwide merchandising services to primarily to grocery stores, said its syndicated services will likely decline 20 to 25 percent through the remainder of the year. But because its commitments are negotiated at fixed prices, the costs of syndicated services will not decline.
Revenues from project work and dedicated services should increase in 1997, but the profits from these two areas will not offset losses in syndicated operations, PIA said.

"We believe this change is representative of an evolving relationship between the retailer and the manufacturer, and we continue to see a higher level of interest in dedicated services," said Clint Owens, chief executive officer.
Owens said Tom Goss, its president and chief operating officer has resigned and John Colwell, a company director will be assisting Owens while PIA searches for a replacement.
Meanwhile, Owens said the company's financial condition remains strong with $23 million in cash, no debt and shareholder's equity of $36.5 million.
